# Introduction

Post-mortem tissue from GTEx and similar resources is the usual "normal" control when a tumour cohort has no adjacent normal tissue. Those donors died in different ways: on a ventilator in intensive care (Hardy scale 0), suddenly (Hardy 1-2) or after a slow illness (Hardy 3-4), and their organs were collected hours after death. `thanatome` carries three consensus transcriptional signatures of those processes, derived from GTEx v8 across ten tissues, and uses them to annotate every sample of a cohort before any downstream analysis:

- **ventilator**: ventilated versus non-ventilated donors; seen from outside GTEx it is the axis *perfused versus post-mortem*;
- **ischemia**: post-mortem ischemic time, meaningful among perfused donors;
- **agony**: slow versus fast deaths among non-ventilated donors.

For each sample the package returns a score per axis, a position scaled between the two poles of the reference tissue, a state label and technical flags. The user can then plot the cohort, select samples with explicit criteria, or carry the scores into a design matrix.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("thanatome")
```

# Scoring a cohort

The example data are 74 GTEx v8 ovary controls and 40 TCGA-OV primary tumours from recount3, with raw counts of the signature genes, the full library size of each sample and the Hardy scale of each donor. The controls are scored first; the tumours enter later, when the differential expression is repeated with different control subsets.

```{r score}
library(thanatome)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
data(thanatome_example)
thanatome_example
ctl <- thanatome_example[, thanatome_example$group == "control"]
table(hardy = ctl$hardy)
```

A reference of the same tissue is mandatory: the scores are means of per-gene z-scores, and a sample has no z-score on its own. For GTEx-like data the package carries the reference of ten tissues.

```{r score2}
sc <- thanatome_score(ctl, reference = "ovary")
sc[1:5, c("ventilator", "ischemia", "agony", "position_ventilator", "position_agony", "state")]
```

Because the example carries the Hardy scale, the function reports as an internal check how well each score recovers the label:

```{r auc}
metadata(sc)$auc
metadata(sc)$state_agreement
```

The scaled position is 0 at the median of the ventilated donors of the reference tissue and 1 at the median of the non-ventilated ones (for agony, 0 = fast deaths, 1 = slow deaths). Values outside 0-1 are allowed: living tissue falls below 0 on the ventilator axis.

# Looking at the samples

```{r plot}
plot_thanatome(sc, hardy = ctl$hardy)
```

```{r ranked}
plot_thanatome(sc, type = "ranked")
```

# Selecting samples with explicit criteria

`select_samples()` applies intervals on the positions, a set of allowed state labels and the technical flags, and reports what was excluded and why. There is no default criterion: in the analyses behind the package no subset of post-mortem controls was closer to surgical or living tissue than the full set except, slightly, the ventilated donors, and every exclusion costs power. The two presets correspond to the criteria the evidence supports as explicit choices, each with its cost documented in the help page.

```{r select}
sel <- select_samples(sc, agony = c(-Inf, 0.5))
sel$summary
head(sel$excluded)
keep <- ctl[, sel$keep]
keep
```

# Using the scores as covariates

The scores can enter a design matrix or `limma::removeBatchEffect()` as continuous covariates. Two cautions apply: the axes vary only among post-mortem samples, so in a tumour-versus-control design adjust within controls or keep the group term; and the adjustment centres the controls at their mean, not at the living pole.

```{r covariates}
cv <- death_covariates(sc)
head(cv)
```

```{r limma, eval = requireNamespace("limma", quietly = TRUE)}
logcpm <- edgeR::cpm(assay(ctl), lib.size = ctl$lib_size, log = TRUE, prior.count = 1)
adjusted <- limma::removeBatchEffect(logcpm, covariates = cv)
dim(adjusted)
```

# Joint regression and the fraction explained

With `method = "regression"` the sample's z profile is regressed jointly on the consensus vectors of the axes. This adds the coefficients and the fraction of the sample's deviation from the tissue centroid explained by the axes (over the signature genes; over the whole transcriptome only with a cohort reference, which covers all genes). Classification is the same as with the signature score; what the regression adds is the fraction explained, which is small (under 1 percent of the whole transcriptome in median) and larger in fast non-ventilated deaths than in the other two states.

```{r regression}
rg <- thanatome_score(ctl, reference = ctl, method = "regression")
summary(rg$r2_signature)
tapply(rg$r2_total, ctl$hardy, median)
```

# A decision workflow for including or excluding controls

The natural loop is: score the samples, filter, look at the differential expression or the master-regulator analysis, and filter again. Its weakness is that the last step selects on the outcome: a filter kept because "the DE looks better" is a filter fitted to the result. `compare_controls()` turns the loop into one pass. The candidate criteria are declared first; each one is run once; every result is compared with the one obtained with all controls **and** with random subsets of the same size, which are the yardstick for what losing samples does by itself. A criterion whose losses and gains do not exceed those of the random subsets acts through sample size, not through the death axes.

```{r compare}
set.seed(1)
cc <- compare_controls(thanatome_example, group = "group", control = "control",
                       criteria = list(perfused = list(preset = "perfused"),
                                       no_agony = list(preset = "no_agony")),
                       reference = "ovary", n_random = 3)
as.data.frame(cc$summary)
```

The same comparison can carry a master-regulator analysis: pass as `mra` a function that takes the DE table of one run and returns a named vector of regulator activities (a wrapper around viper or NaRnEA); the agreement of each criterion with the full set, and of the random subsets, is added to the summary. The regulators themselves can be annotated with `annotate_mra()`, which reports how much of each regulon lies in the death axes and in which direction.

```{r mra}
sig <- thanatome_firmas("ventilator")
regs <- list(TF_vent = list(tfmode = setNames(rep(1, 30), sig$ensembl[sig$direction == "up"][1:30])),
             TF_other = paste0("ENSG0000000", seq_len(40)))
annotate_mra(c(TF_vent = 3.1, TF_other = 0.2), regs, axes = c("ventilator", "agony"))
```

`audit_report()` writes the whole thing as text for a supplement.

```{r report}
rep <- audit_report(sc, selection = select_samples(sc, preset = "no_agony"), comparison = cc)
```

# Annotating an existing differential-expression table

`annotate_de()` adds to each gene the axis and direction it falls in, the consensus log fold change and the change in the tumour-versus-control log fold change expected when the control subset moves from non-ventilated to ventilated donors (or from fast to slow deaths), which within GTEx equals the contrast between the two subsets of controls.

```{r annotate}
sig <- thanatome_firmas("ventilator")
de <- data.frame(logFC = c(0.2, 2.5, -1), adj.P.Val = c(0.01, 0.001, 0.04),
                 row.names = c(sig$ensembl[1], sig$ensembl[2], "ENSG00000000003"))
annotate_de(de, axes = c("ventilator", "agony"))
```
